title: Someone is threatening or harassing me online: what you can do now
pageTitle: Someone is threatening or harassing me online: what you can do now | Spamlock
description: Blackmail over private photos (sextortion), harassment, or your home address or phone number posted online (doxxing)? Steps you can take now: stop replying, keep evidence, block, report and get free help.
answer: Stop replying, and don’t pay if someone is blackmailing you. Take screenshots first, then block and report them. It’s not your fault, and free help is available.
stepsTitle: Steps you can take if someone is threatening or harassing you online

steps.title: Stop replying
steps.text: Replying keeps the pressure on. Stopping contact shows them you won’t give in.

steps.title: Blackmailed over private photos? Don’t pay
steps.text: Paying usually leads to more demands. If you already paid, it’s not too late to stop all contact and block them.

steps.title: Save the evidence first
steps.text: Take screenshots of the messages and posts, and note the username, the app or website, and the date. Do this before you block.

steps.title: Block and report
steps.text: Block the account, and report it to the app or website. If a new account contacts you, do the same again.

steps.title: Get private photos taken down
steps.text: Free tools help stop them being shared on many big platforms, without anyone seeing your photos.

steps.title: Your details posted online?
steps.text: Report the post to the website or app, and make your social accounts private.

steps.title: Report it to the police
steps.text: Give them your screenshots and notes.

steps.title: Talk to someone
steps.text: In the UK, adults can contact the Revenge Porn Helpline for free help with private photos.
